questions.question: Biological Oxygen demand (BOD) measures

options.text: The amount of oxidizable organic matter present in water body
The amount of oxygen dissolved in water, air and soil.
The amount of total inorganic matter present in water body
The amount of organic and inorganic matter present in water body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The amount of oxidizable organic matter present in water body.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD):

 
 
• Biological Oxygen Demand is the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by microorganisms to decompose organic matter (waste or pollutants) under aerobic reaction (in the presence of oxygen). Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• The more organic matter there is (e.g., in sewage and polluted bodies of water), the greater is the BOD. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.
 
• Greater BOD, the lower the amount of dissolved oxygen available for higher animals such as fishes. Hence, statement 3 is not correct.
 
• The BOD is therefore a reliable gauge of the organic pollution of a water body.
 
• One of the main reasons for treating wastewater prior to its discharge into a water resource is to lower its BOD i.e. to reduce its need for oxygen and thereby lessen its demand from the streams, lakes, rivers, or estuaries into which it is released.
 
 
 
• Dissolved Oxygen:
 
 
• It is the amount of dissolved oxygen present in the water which is needed for aquatic life to survive.
 
• The quality of water increases with an increase in DO levels.
 
• A DO level of 5 mg/l or above is the recommended level for bathing in a river.

questions.question: Who has the authorization for the withdrawal of funds from the Consolidated Fund of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Parliament of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **Article 114** of the Constitution, the government can only remove funds from the Consolidated Fund with Parliament's consent.

 
 
• ​The Appropriation Bill grants the government the authority to take money out of the Consolidated Fund of India to cover expenses during the fiscal year. 
 
• After debates over budget ideas and votes on grant requests, the appropriations bill is presented to the Lok Sabha.
 
• A government would resign or call a general election if an appropriations bill was defeated in a vote in parliament.
 
 
 
• The three divisions into which the Indian government's funds are divided are as follows:
 
 
• *Consolidated Fund of India*
 
• *Contingency Fund of India*
 
• *Public Accounts of India*
 
 
 
• **The Consolidated Fund of India is the most crucial.**
 
 
• Both direct and indirect taxes replenish this fund, as well as the Indian government's borrowings, and anyone or whatever agency has borrowed the money must return it along with the interest to the government.
 
• All of the government's expenses are covered by this fund.
 
• To take money out of this fund, ***the government need parliamentary authorization.***
 
• In **Article 266(1)** of the Indian Constitution, this fund is mentioned.
 
• Each state is allowed to have a Consolidated Fund of its own with corresponding rules.
 
• These funds are audited by the **Comptroller and Auditor General of India**, who also provides management information to the appropriate legislatures.

questions.question: When the 'direct action' was started by muslim league ?
questions.solution:
The 'direct action' was started by Muslim League on **16 august, 1946**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **March 1946** the **British cabinet** sent a **three-member mission to Delhi **to examine the **demand for Pakistan by Muslim League** and to suggest a suitable political framework for a free India.
 
• This mission suggested that India should remain united and constitute itself as a loose confederation with some autonomy for Muslim-majority areas.
 
• But it could not get the **Congress and the Muslim League **to agree to specific details of the proposal.
 
• Partition now became more or less inevitable.
 
• After the failure of the **Cabinet Mission**, the **Muslim League** decided on **mass agitation** for winning its **Pakistan demand.**
 
• It announced **16 August 1946** as “**Direct Action Day**”.
 
• 
 
On this day riots broke out in Calcutta, lasting several days and resulting in the death of thousands of people. 

 

Hence, we can conclude that the 'direct action' was started by Muslim League on 16 august, 1946.

questions.question: What is the name of the recently conducted Military exercise between India and Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Mitra Shakti.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The ninth edition of India-Sri Lanka Joint Military exercise “**Exercise MITRA SHAKTI-2023**” commenced today in Aundh, **Pune**.

• The aim of the exercise is to jointly rehearse conduct of Sub Conventional operations under Chapter VII of United Nations Charter.

questions.question: A Writ of Mandamus is an order issued by the Supreme Court or High Courts to:

options.text: a lower court to transfer a case to a higher court.
a public official or government authority to perform a duty they are legally obligated to complete
the Parliament to enact or repeal a specific law
an individual to prohibit them from entering into a private contract

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mandamus: "We command” -** directs a public authority or government official to perform a duty that is mandated by law, ensuring lawful action. Hence, option 2 is correct.
 
• **Habeas Corpus: "Produce the body" –** A writ used to ensure a person unlawfully detained is brought before the court to check the legality of the detention.
 
• **Prohibition:** Issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal, preventing it from proceeding with a case beyond its jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari: "To be certified" –** Transferred from a lower court to a higher court for reviewing and correcting an error in a case where the lower court exceeded its jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** "By what authority" – Challenges a person’s right to hold a public office, asking them to show the authority by which they occupy the position.

questions.question: The Mahalanobis model was the basis for which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Second Five-yea Plan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahalanobis model was the basis for the Second Five-Year Plan of India, which took place from 1956–1961: 
 
• The Mahalanobis model was an economic development model created by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.
 
• The model was based on an input-output model and was used to establish the plan's goals and priorities.
 
• The plan's goals included: Rapid industrialization, Development of the public sector, Balanced allocation of investment between productive sectors, and A 25% increase in national income. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Second Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan in India was from 1956 to 1961.
 
• The plan's main objectives were to develop heavy industries and construct railway lines in the northeast. 
 
 
 
• Sixth Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The Sixth Five-Year Plan in India was from 1980 to 1985.
 
• The plan's objectives were to increase national income, modernize technology, and reduce poverty and unemployment. 
 
 
 
• First Five-Year Plan
 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan in India was from 1951 to 1956.
 
• The plan was based on the Harrod-Domar Model and focused on agriculture.

questions.question: In Sun-Earth system, the Sun, the Earth and the Lagrange point L4 form:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *__**an equilateral triangle**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Sun-Earth System and Lagrange Points**

__
 
• The **Sun-Earth system** consists of the Sun, the Earth, and several points in space where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth create a stable environment for objects to reside.
 
• **Lagrange points** are positions where the gravitational pull of two large bodies, like the Earth and the Sun, precisely equals the centripetal force felt by a smaller object.
 
• In the **Sun-Earth system**, there are five Lagrange points, namely **L1, L2, L3, L4, and L5**.
 
• The **L4 and L5 points** form an equilateral triangle with the two large bodies, which in this case are the Sun and the Earth.
 
• These points are located at a **60-degree angle** ahead of and behind the Earth in its orbit around the Sun.
 
• **L4 and L5** are considered stable because objects located there tend to stay put, making them ideal for space missions and satellites.

**Explanation of the Correct Answer**

 
• The Sun, the Earth, and the Lagrange point **L4** form an **equilateral triangle**. This is due to the **stable gravitational environment** created by the Sun and Earth's combined gravitational forces.
 
• An **equilateral triangle** has all three sides of equal length and all three angles equal to **60 degrees**. This geometric configuration ensures that the gravitational forces and the centripetal force are balanced.
 
• In the context of the Sun-Earth system, the **L4** point is located at a point where the gravitational pull from both the Sun and the Earth creates a stable environment for objects to reside.
 
• The configuration of the **L4** point forming an equilateral triangle with the Sun and the Earth is a direct consequence of the **gravitational equilibrium** achieved at this point.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **an equilateral triangle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lagrange Points**:

 
 
• Named after the Italian-French mathematician **Joseph-Louis Lagrange**, who discovered them in **1772**.
 
• These points are solutions to the restricted three-body problem, where two large bodies influence a third, much smaller body.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Lagrange Points**:
 
 
• The **L1 point** is used for solar observation satellites like the **Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)**.
 
• The **L2 point** is ideal for space telescopes, such as the **James Webb Space Telescope**, due to its stable environment and minimal shadowing from the Earth and Moon.
 
• The **L4 and L5 points** are considered for potential space habitats or as locations for space colonies due to their stability.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Equilibrium**:
 
 
• Objects at Lagrange points are in a state of gravitational equilibrium, meaning the forces acting on them are balanced.
 
• This equilibrium allows for minimal fuel consumption for station-keeping, making these points advantageous for long-term space missions.

questions.question: In which of the following years, did Mahatma Gandhi propose the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1937.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• In **1937__**, __**Mahatma Gandh**__i proposed the __**Wardha Scheme of Basic Education.**__

 __
 
• The **Wardha Education **Plan was the name given to it.
 
• It was intended that all children between the ages of **8 and 14 **should have access to **free**, **public education **in their **native tongues**.
 
• **Nai Talim,** or the **New Education**, became the name for this. 
 
• The purpose of fundamental education was to foster the **virtues **of the **ideal citizen**, and greater emphasis should be placed on **Indian culture **than **literacy**.
 
• **English **should have no room in the **curriculum**.
 
• In this plan, **religious instruction **has **no place.**
 
• The most crucial aspect was the economic objectives of the fundamental education, which would be developed over the course of **seven years **by the **kids**' **manual labour**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• On **October 22 **and **23**, **1937**, the **Wardha Education Conference **took place, and the following three **fundamental resolutions **were adopted:

 
 
• 7 years of the **nationwide**, **free **and **required education.**
 
• **Mother Tongue **shall be the **Instructional Medium.**
 
• Not only for **degrees **and **exams** but also for **physical **or **productive employment**, education will be **prioritised**. As a result, it combined **craft work**, **social environment**, and **physical environment**.
 
 
 
• A **committee **led by **Dr Zakir Hussain** was constituted as a result of this conference in **Wardha**.
 
• The **Wardha Scheme of Basic Education**, which the **Committee **submitted as part of its report in **March 1938**, was the **first comprehensive national basic education programme.**
